title: Do You Need Restaurant Reservations in Berlin? - Quick Summary
items: **The Berlin default is to walk in.** Most restaurants, cafes and every Imbiss expect you to just turn up. For a normal weeknight in a normal neighbourhood, do not book anything.
**Reserve when your table is five or more.** Big groups are the single biggest reason to book anywhere in Berlin, and walk-in luck runs out fast once the table gets long.
**Book buzzy names, special meals and Friday or Saturday nights.** A place you could stroll into on a Tuesday can be full by eight on a busy weekend.

**Berlin has no single booking app.** Check Google Maps for a Reserve a table button first, then the restaurant's own site. Traditional German houses often still take tables by phone or email, and plenty of casual places take no reservations at all.
**Sundays are quieter than you expect.** Fewer kitchens run and brunch spots fill up, so check a place is open before you set out and treat popular Sunday spots like a weekend booking.
**Terraces and beer gardens are first-come.** On a warm evening, arrive early rather than expecting to reserve a bench.
